focus.product: Machined and pressed motorcycle and car components (tier-2 parts for Astra-group OEMs)
focus.why: Kab. Tegal's 2022–2042 industry plan names motorcycle components, metal goods, machinery and casting as priority industries in Talang/Adiwerna. About 70 YDBA-coached metal SMEs, 16 already supplying AHM, TAM, ADM and Suzuki at tier 2 (Feb 2024). Named suppliers: FNF Metalindo (70–80 items), Bimuda (70 items), Dharmapoli. Indonesia imported US$635m of motorcycle parts in 2025, 57% from China.

also.product: Ship fittings built to BKI class: windows, watertight doors, gate valves, fire-hose couplings and nozzles
also.why: Tegal SMEs won Indonesia's first SME BKI class certificates (ship windows, doors, fire-hose connections and nozzles) in March 2015, when about 70% of shipyard components were imported. PT Karya Manunggal Manufaktur holds TKDN certificates for ship windows and watertight doors. The regency plan lists ship components as a priority industry. In 2025 Indonesia imported US$35.4m of steel doors and windows (730830) and US$944.8m of other valves (848180). HS codes are my mapping.

also.product: Power-distribution line hardware for the PLN network (cross arms, transformer brackets, clamps, fuse-holder sets)
also.why: Three Tegal firms hold TKDN certificates for network hardware: Logam Jaya Sejahtera (18 products, 40–100%), Benko Metalindo Prima (FCO fuse holder, 94.72%) and Berkah Aneka Logam (brackets, 38–40%). This is a captive state-utility market that rewards local content. In 2025 imports were US$219.1m for other iron/steel articles (732690) and US$4.4m for HV fuses (853510). Sheet CNC (cutting, punching, bending) fits; HS codes are my mapping.

skills: Kab. Tegal (Dalam Angka 2022, in RPIK): 2 polytechnics, 1 academy, 4 sekolah tinggi, 7 public and 57 private SMKs, 1 BLK, 57 LPK. Politeknik Harapan Bersama's campus now belongs to Universitas Harkat Negeri. Universitas Pancasakti and Disnakerin ran CNC-turning training at SILKOT (snippet).

focus.product: Moulds for rubber and plastics (tyre, shoe-sole and injection moulds), plus jigs and maintenance spares for KEK Kendal and KEK Batang tenants
focus.why: Both SEZs host mould-using plants. Kendal: ZC Rubber and Matahari Tire, appliance makers, Polygroup. Batang: Yih Quan Footwear, Wavin pipes, Unipack (snippet). The local machining base is thin (36 machine shops in Pekalongan, 8 in Batang, none listed in Kendal; directory, Apr 2026). Indonesia imported US$214m of injection/compression moulds (848071) in 2025, 68% from China. 3D printing serves prototypes and patterns.

also.product: CNC-routed furniture parts and panels for SEZ furniture plants
also.why: PT Woodpark Mebel Perkasa is building a Rp225bn plant in KEK Batang (operating April 2027) for B&B Italia, Arhaus and Restoration Hardware. Kemenperin's Politeknik Industri Furnitur sits inside the Kendal estate (Rp125bn, 2019). Batang's RPIK lists furniture as a priority industry.

also.product: Fishing-vessel propellers, shafts and deck fittings
also.why: The provincial plan assigns the ship industry to Kab. Pekalongan and Batang, and Batang's plan lists shipyards as a potential. A Batang wooden-boat builder (CV Anugrah Jaya Bahari) holds a TKDN certificate. Indonesia imported US$27.7m of propellers in 2025. Low-confidence pick: no fleet or shipyard counts were found.

focus.product: Food-service and food-processing equipment and parts (stoves, ovens, dish dryers, food machines)
focus.why: Bugangan metal centre: 56 SMEs making food-processing machines and household equipment (2018). TKDN-certified Semarang makers of gas stoves (Niko Elektronik, Cipta Gagah Perkasa), ovens (Hadeka) and dish dryers (Soraya Bumi Kita). Semarang has the region's densest base: 127 machine shops and 33 laser-cutting services (directory, Apr 2026). Indonesia imported US$316.8m of 8438 machinery and US$69.1m of 841981 in 2025. Gas stoves (732111) are already a net export (US$66.5m exported against US$2.1m imported).

also.product: Diesel-engine and tractor components for Kubota Indonesia's Semarang plant
also.why: Kubota builds horizontal diesel engines and 4-wheel tractors at BSB, with TKDN certificates at 25–72%. Raising local content needs local machined castings, shafts and gears (inference). PT Aegis Jaya Metalindo (castings, TKDN 100%) is in nearby KIW. Indonesia imported US$342m of diesel-engine parts (840999) in 2025.

also.product: 3D-printing and prototyping services (product prototypes, jigs, patterns)
also.why: Semarang has 21 of the 178 3D-printing services listed in Central Java (directory, Apr 2026) and Polines' CNC and EDM labs. It is the region's design and university hub. Not a traded product.

focus.product: CNC-routed furniture components and carved panels for Jepara's furniture exporters
focus.why: Jepara has 387 large exporting carving firms and 3,438 small carving units; carving is about 34.5% of regional GDP (2020 data). In Aug 2026 the Jepara wood-craftsmen association said labour is scarce and the work split is about 50:50 labour to machine, heading for 80% machine. Indonesia exported US$696m of wooden furniture (940360), US$58m of 4420 wood articles and US$34.8m of wooden furniture parts (940391) in 2025.

also.product: Small agricultural machinery (threshers, corn shellers, dryers, rice-milling units) and their machined parts
also.why: Five Kudus/Pati makers hold TKDN certificates, mostly at 40–58%: Pura Barutama, Mandiri Garlica Pratama, Athoose Jaya Agritech, Sarana Agro Tekindo and Javatech Agro Persada. Indonesia imported US$187.5m of harvesting/threshing machinery (8433) in 2025, 77% from China. It also imported US$10.3m of other threshers (843352) and US$9.5m of agricultural dryers (841934). HS codes are my mapping.

also.product: Juwana brass hardware and fittings (door handles, lamp parts, stove, pump and compressor parts): 3D-printed casting patterns plus CNC finishing
also.why: Juwana has a brass cluster dating to Daendels' era (238 units, 68 registered SMEs, 2009 data). It sand-casts scrap brass with manual lathes, and products are exported (2018 study). Sampurna Brass is among its larger firms. In 2025 Indonesia imported US$63.8m of base-metal building fittings (830241; exports US$15.5m) and US$28.3m of other copper articles (741980). Data are old; HS codes are my mapping.
